failed_hard_gates.evidence: The tool hand is visibly continuous through its wrist and forearm into the screen-right sleeve, and the detached assembly is clearly robot-owned. The support fingers/palm at approximately x570-774,y681-816 and thumb x660-727,y590-633 contact the bare mid-frame. The support sleeve/skin patch at x491-592,y550-590 disappears behind the top rail and internal actuator; the complete support wrist-to-forearm contour is not traceable together. This required route is unobservable, not evidence of a hidden deformity.

The robot upper segment, large circular elbow at x192-425,y509-744, open frame x408-1009,y573-787 and separate wrist near x1006-1119,y692-830 form a distinct connected mechanical chain. The driver reach is clear. However the frozen complete human support-hand wrist/forearm route is partly behind the frame, so the complete combined joint/reach check cannot pass despite the robot-specific chain passing.

The face/hair, robot chassis, two work hands, whole detached robot arm, separate elbow/frame/wrist and driver endpoint all share the original frame, and the repaired machine/contact details are readable. The support wrist-to-forearm route required by the explicit continuity clause remains partly behind the mechanical rail/actuator. Whole-scene visibility therefore fails even though the targeted robot and contact components are visible.
